verdict: The engine is not broken, it is diluted, and it has one uncovered hole. Across 1411 replayed trades the whole book earns +70.59R at PF 1.09 and expectancy 0.065R against an assumed cost of 0.05R -- essentially nothing net of costs. That blended number hides one real edge and a pile of taxes on it: MOMENTUM alone is +156.31R over 623 closed at PF 1.37 and is profitable in every adequately-sampled regime slice (TRENDING 0.228 / RANGING 0.325 / SQUEEZE 0.403), while eight of ten setups are net negative. The book is a long, strong-uptrend machine (BUY +135.01R vs SELL -64.42R; STRONG UPTREND +158.82R with every other trend bucket negative). Three loss clusters carry nearly all the drag and they overlap by an unmeasured amount: SPX (-85.5R, PF 0.27, 12.6% win over 127 closed -- larger in magnitude than the entire book's profit, and strategySettings has no per-symbol kill switch at all), BREAKDOWN taken at MODERATE strength (-45.77R over 145 closed at PF 0.61, while BREAKDOWN|STRONG runs +1.034R expectancy), and the five-to-six setups with no profitable adequately-sampled slice in any strength or regime. Meanwhile executionDisabledSetups is empty, breakdownEnabled is true, minEntryRsi is 0, and the system's own feedback loop is vacuous: 15 journal entries and 4 setups on disk against 1411 replayed trades, an aiFilter health check reporting ok=true precisely because it has never once run, healCount 0, and a live learning file that records MOMENTUM as net negative on five trades and carries a setup name (BB_SQUEEZE_WATCH) plus an UNATTRIBUTED bucket that exist nowhere in the executed record. So the system cannot see any of this by itself, and the single knob it is permitted to auto-tune (adxTrendingMin) points at the one dimension where the data shows no separation at all.

actions.action: Stop executing SPX. Add a per-symbol execution blocklist to strategySettings mirroring executionDisabledSetups -- it does not exist today, executionDisabledSetups is setup-scoped only -- and put SPX in it. In parallel, open a defect investigation into why SPX loses this badly (contract/point-value spec, stop distance in points vs price, data feed, session hours) before treating the block as permanent.
actions.rationale: byAsset SPX: 127 closed, 16W/111L, 12.6% win, PF 0.27, -85.5R, expectancy -0.673R. That single stream is larger in magnitude than the whole book's +70.59R, and it is 3-5x worse than BTC (PF 1.19, +72.17R over 562 closed) or Gold (PF 1.31, +83.92R over 391 closed) running the same logic. A 12.6% win rate against 33-35% on the other two assets is not a strategy-quality difference; it is the signature of something structurally wrong on that symbol, which is why the code investigation is part of the action rather than optional.
actions.measurableWhy: The replay already tags every trade by asset (coverage BTC 682 / Gold 485 / SPX 244), so re-scoring the book with SPX excluded is a pure post-filter on existing output and needs no new replay capability. The enforcement mechanism itself sits in the signal-to-execution path outside generateSignal, so the replay measures the effect, not the gate.
actions.agreement: loss-autopsy and risk-and-config propose it independently and both rank it the largest single drain; no analyst argues against it. setup-forensics, strength-gate and regime-fit did not analyse the asset dimension at all, so this is 2-for, 0-against, 3 silent.
actions.risk: Only 127 of SPX's 244 trades are closed (52%), so the closed subset may be selection-biased. You lose one of three markets of diversification. And if the cause is a spec or data defect, blocking the symbol hides the bug instead of fixing it -- hence the bundled investigation. Note also that SPX's -85.5R overlaps unknown amounts with the BREAKDOWN and RSI<50 losses below: savings from actions 1, 2, 3 and 7 are NOT additive.

actions.action: Add a per-setup minimum-strength floor in the entry gate (checked after setup classification, falling back to the global minStrength when a setup is unlisted) and seed it with BREAKDOWN = STRONG. Leave global minStrength at MODERATE. If that code cannot ship immediately, set breakdownEnabled=false as an explicitly time-boxed interim, not as the answer.
actions.rationale: setupByStrength BREAKDOWN|MODERATE is 145 closed, 22.1% win, PF 0.61, -45.77R, expectancy -0.316R -- the largest single loss cell in the pack. BREAKDOWN|STRONG is 11 closed, 63.6% win, PF 3.71, +11.37R, expectancy +1.034R (belowMinSample=false against the floor of 5). The strength split removes more loss than the regime split does (-45.77R over 145 closed vs BREAKDOWN|TRENDING's -28.4R over 116 closed) and it is the only cut that preserves a positive residual, so it strictly dominates both the regime gate and the blunt disable.
actions.measurableWhy: Setup classification and signal strength are both outputs of generateSignal over historical bars, so the replay can re-run with the floor applied and report the new bySetup/setupByStrength directly. This is the cleanest item in the list to validate before shipping.
actions.agreement: Four of five. setup-forensics, strength-gate, loss-autopsy and risk-and-config all independently identify BREAKDOWN|MODERATE as the avoidable cell and all four name the per-setup strength floor as the preferred implementation with breakdownEnabled=false as the blunt fallback. regime-fit agrees BREAKDOWN must be cut but proposes a regime gate instead -- see disagreements.
actions.risk: BREAKDOWN|STRONG rests on 11 closed trades: past the sample floor of 5 but thin, so +1.034R expectancy is fragile, and the surviving branch fires so rarely (17 of 210 BREAKDOWN signals were STRONG) that it will take a long time to re-prove itself. Cutting the MODERATE leg also removes most of the book's remaining short-side volume, deepening an already heavy long bias. The interim breakdownEnabled=false forfeits the +11.37R and is strictly worse-targeted.

gate.detail: per-setup strength map (new) / breakdownEnabled (interim only) is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Populate executionDisabledSetups, currently empty, with the setups that have no profitable adequately-sampled slice in any strength or regime. Ship in two tranches: tranche A (well-sampled, unambiguous) RANGE_TRADE_SHORT and RANGE_TRADE_LONG; tranche B (thinner, only after A is verified) BUY_OVERSOLD, SELL_BOUNCE, BREAKOUT and SQUEEZE_BREAKOUT. Hold BUY_DIP and TREND_FOLLOW live-but-watched.
actions.rationale: Tranche A: RANGE_TRADE_SHORT -18.49R over 65 closed (PF 0.63) is negative in all three adequately-sampled regimes (RANGING -0.352 / SQUEEZE -0.621 / TRENDING -0.130) and has no STRONG leg to retreat to; RANGE_TRADE_LONG -10.13R over 43 closed (PF 0.68) is negative in TRENDING -0.468, RANGING -0.197 and SQUEEZE -0.031, also MODERATE-only. Tranche B: BUY_OVERSOLD -9.77R/26 closed (PF 0.53, worst expectancy in the pack at -0.376), SELL_BOUNCE -4.88R/22 closed (PF 0.73), BREAKOUT -5.39R/21 closed (PF 0.70), and SQUEEZE_BREAKOUT -7.7R/84 closed (PF 0.88) whose best slice, |TRENDING at +0.050 expectancy, is exactly the costAssumptionR of 0.05 -- zero net of costs, so gating it to TRENDING buys nothing that disabling does not. Hold BUY_DIP (-0.62R over only 11 closed, effectively breakeven) and TREND_FOLLOW (+5.66R over 29 closed, PF 1.30).
actions.measurableWhy: Setup labels come from generateSignal's setup logic, which the replay sees directly, so each tranche can be scored by re-running or by post-filtering the existing 1411-trade output before any of it goes live.
actions.agreement: All five, with different list boundaries. setup-forensics proposes the range setups plus BUY_OVERSOLD, SELL_BOUNCE and BREAKOUT; strength-gate proposes the same core two then widening to five; regime-fit proposes RANGE_TRADE_SHORT specifically and argues no regime rescues it; risk-and-config proposes the range setups plus BUY_OVERSOLD; loss-autopsy corroborates via its bearish-bucket analysis. The two-setup core is backed by every analyst who addressed setups.
actions.risk: Tranche B rests on 21-26 closed trades per setup -- above the sample floor of 5 but thin enough that a bad run rather than a structural defect could be doing the work. Together with actions 1 and 2 this strips roughly 300 closed trades of flow at exactly the moment the learning engine needs volume, and concentrates the book almost entirely into MOMENTUM (623 of the remaining closed trades), a single point of failure if that edge decays. A hard disable also never self-corrects: if the losses are window-specific rather than structural, nothing will tell you.

gate.detail: executionDisabledSetups is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Raise confidenceThreshold from 70 to 80, staged via 75, and hold it for a fixed evaluation window rather than reverting on the first quiet week.
actions.rationale: byConfidence conf>=80: 226 closed, 37.6% win, PF 1.50, +74.52R, expectancy 0.33R. conf70-79: 267 closed, 33.0% win, PF 1.19, +36.64R, expectancy 0.137R. The band the current gate admits earns under half the expectancy of the band above it, and 0.137R against a 0.05R cost assumption is a thin real edge. The bands below the gate (conf65-69 -3.78R, conf<50 -47.5R) confirm the score has genuine signal at the top end even though it is non-monotonic in the middle. This is a one-line config change with 226 closed trades behind it.
actions.measurableWhy: The replay runs generateSignal, which does not apply confidenceThreshold -- that gate lives downstream. The byConfidence buckets give a static historical attribution of what the >=80 population did, but the replay cannot re-run the system under a different threshold, so second-order effects (which setups survive, how the surviving mix interacts with actions 1-3) stay unmeasured. Treat +0.33R as an upper-bound estimate, not a simulated result.
actions.agreement: risk-and-config proposes it directly. loss-autopsy reaches the same boundary from the other side, noting the live threshold of 70 already excludes the worst bands so the 70-79 band is the only remaining lever. setup-forensics, strength-gate and regime-fit did not analyse the confidence dimension.
actions.risk: Cuts signal count sharply on top of actions 1-3, pushing volume far under maxTradesPerDay=10 and making weekly results noisy and slow to evaluate. The >=80 bucket has 360 signals but only 226 closed (63%), so its measured edge may shrink as the rest close. Stacking this with the setup disables and the RSI floor could cut volume far more than any single estimate implies.

gate.detail: confidenceThreshold is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Reject any signal in the DAILY+H4_CONFLICT cohort -- if the daily and H4 directions disagree, do not execute. Implement as an explicit cohort gate; do not try to approximate it with dailyOnlyMinConfidence, which points at a different cohort.
actions.rationale: byCohort DAILY+H4_CONFLICT: 43 closed, 5W/38L, 11.6% win, PF 0.20, -31.87R, expectancy -0.741R -- the worst expectancy of any adequately-sampled cohort in the pack. The contrast is decisive: DAILY+H4_AGREE is 214 closed at PF 1.45 and +64.12R, and even the weak DAILY_ONLY_H4_NEUTRAL cohort (19.7% win) is net positive at PF 1.03. Low win rate alone is therefore not the problem; active timeframe disagreement is. dailyOnlyMinConfidence=0 currently aims at the near-breakeven cohort, not this one.
actions.measurableWhy: Timeframe agreement is computed in generateSignalMTF, which the replay does not run -- it calls generateSignal only. The byCohort labels let you attribute historical R to the cohort after the fact, but the replay cannot re-run the gate or show the book with the cohort removed and everything else re-derived. You can subtract, not simulate.
actions.agreement: loss-autopsy and risk-and-config propose the identical gate and both explicitly reject dailyOnlyMinConfidence as the wrong lever. The other three did not examine the cohort dimension.
actions.risk: 43 closed trades is a modest base for a permanent hard block. If the cohort label is computed differently in the live path than in whatever produced these labels, the gate could silently reject a far wider set than intended -- verify the live label matches before shipping. Conflict-cohort signals may also be the system's only participation at genuine trend turns.

actions.action: Fix the feedback loop so the system can see its own state: make healer.checks.aiFilter report degraded while it has never evaluated a trade; make learningFile and journalFile compare on-disk counts against executed trade count instead of merely asserting the file exists; reconcile setup attribution between the live path and the replay/journal path (BB_SQUEEZE_WATCH and XAUUSD/UNATTRIBUTED appear in the learning file but in no executed record); and confirm in code that nothing gates or throttles execution on learning.setupStats P&L.
actions.rationale: healer.healthy=true, healCount=0, errorLog empty, every check ok=true -- including aiFilter, whose own detail string reads 'no trade has been evaluated yet, filter unexercised'. That is a check passing by vacuity, exactly the failure mode a healer exists to catch. learningFile is green at 4 setups and journalFile green at 15 entries against 1411 replayed trades. Worse, liveState.learning.setupStats records MOMENTUM as 3W/2L and -170.32 net -- the opposite sign from measured MOMENTUM (+156.31R, PF 1.37, 623 closed) -- on a five-trade sample. If any gate consumes those numbers, the system will suppress the one setup carrying the entire book on the basis of five trades. This action generates no R itself; it is what stops actions 1-5 being silently undone and stops a five-trade sample steering a 623-trade edge.
actions.measurableWhy: This is live-state instrumentation and attribution plumbing. It involves no historical bars and no generateSignal behaviour, so the replay has nothing to say about it either way -- verify by code inspection and unit tests on the healer checks.
actions.agreement: risk-and-config raises all of it (vacuous aiFilter, starved learning file, journal count mismatch, the BB_SQUEEZE_WATCH/UNATTRIBUTED naming inconsistency). strength-gate independently corroborates that live closed volume is near zero and that nothing filters the drag today. The other three did not examine liveState.
actions.risk: A stricter healer will fire on a freshly restarted or genuinely low-volume system, so it needs a grace window and a minimum-volume floor before escalating to a self-heal -- otherwise you have swapped a check that never fires for one that always does. Changing attribution naming risks orphaning existing on-disk learning records; migrate rather than rename in place.

actions.action: Set an entry RSI floor, but first verify in code whether minEntryRsi is applied to BUY signals only or to all directions. If it is direction-blind, make it BUY-only before enabling it. Stage the value at 35, then 45; do not go straight to 50.
actions.rationale: byRsi rsi<35: 193 closed, 25.9% win, PF 0.73, -40.82R. rsi35-50: 129 closed, 27.1% win, PF 0.79, -20.64R. rsi50-65: 442 closed, PF 1.33, +104.7R. rsi>=65: 316 closed, PF 1.13, +27.35R. A combined -61.46R of the closed book sits below RSI 50 and the setting already exists (minEntryRsi=0, limits 0-60), so this is config rather than code -- provided the direction question is settled. Note also that momentumRsiMax and trendFollowRsiMax have both been raised to 100 from defaults of 72 and 68, and the data supports that: rsi>=65 is profitable, so the disabled ceilings are not the problem. The missing floor is.
actions.measurableWhy: Entry RSI is recorded per replayed trade -- the byRsi buckets are built from it -- so a floor can be scored as a post-filter on existing output. The direction-conditional variant needs an RSI-by-direction cross-tab this fact pack does not contain, but the replay can produce one, and it should before this ships.
actions.agreement: regime-fit, loss-autopsy and risk-and-config all propose an RSI floor. loss-autopsy and regime-fit both flag the direction caveat; loss-autopsy states it most sharply. Ranked below the setup work because of that unresolved caveat and because it overlaps heavily with actions 1-3.
actions.risk: The pack never crosses RSI with direction, so an unknown share of the -61.46R below RSI 50 is SELL trades a BUY-only floor will not touch -- realised gain could be far smaller than the headline. A blanket floor applied to shorts would block exactly the low-RSI entries a short setup wants. At 50 it removes 322 closed trades, roughly a third of the closed book, and would suppress BUY_OVERSOLD and BUY_DIP entirely (BUY_OVERSOLD is already disabled in tranche B, so check for double-counting).

gate.detail: minEntryRsi is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Do not let the auto-tuner move adxTrendingMin. Pin it at 20. If you want to know whether the boundary matters, run 20 vs 25 vs 30 as a replay experiment and read the result -- but do not ship a change on the byAdx buckets alone, and widen autoTunableSettings to a knob the data actually discriminates on rather than leaving this as the sole adaptive lever.
actions.rationale: byAdx win rates are 31.5% (adx<20), 32.3% (adx20-30) and 31.0% (adx>=30) -- effectively identical, so ADX carries no win-rate signal. The R profile is a middle-band problem: adx<20 +75.14R at PF 1.33 (the best band), adx20-30 -24.6R at PF 0.92 (the only negative one), adx>=30 +20.05R at PF 1.08. A single threshold cannot isolate a losing band sitting between two profitable ones. Critically, adxTrendingMin is a regime-classification boundary, not a filter: raising it does not remove the 427 trades in the 20-30 band, it relabels them into RANGING/SQUEEZE handling where a different and possibly worse setup mix fires, and it changes the regime label that action 2's gate would consume. Cheap to test in replay, wrong to ship blind.
actions.measurableWhy: This is the one setting the replay can fully see, and the only entry in autoTunableSettings. generateSignal consumes adxTrendingMin directly, so a full re-replay at each value gives a genuine simulated answer including the second-order setup-mix effects -- which is exactly why it should be measured rather than reasoned about.
actions.agreement: loss-autopsy and risk-and-config both argue for freezing it, on the same middle-band logic. regime-fit argues the opposite (raise to 25/28/30) -- see disagreements; the facts favour freezing, and regime-fit's own risk field concedes the reclassification point.
actions.risk: Freezing the only auto-tunable setting removes the system's sole self-adjustment path until a better-supported tunable is added -- an argument for widening autoTunableSettings, not for tuning a knob that shows no separation. Conversely, auto-tuning confidenceThreshold or minStrength instead is far more consequential than a regime label and would chase noise badly on short windows; add them only with a minimum-sample guard.

gate.detail: 30          replay failed: could not extract const MOMENTUM_MACD_EXEMPT_TICKERS from server/index.js â€” refusing to replay, because without it generateSignal throws on every bar and the result would silently be an empty trade |  | No results — nothing to decide.

actions.action: Do not raise frequency or risk until a post-change replay shows the book's PF improving. Specifically: reduce maxTradesPerDay from 10 back toward its default of 5, hold riskPercent at 0.15, maxConcurrentPositions at 3 and maxLotSize at 2, and keep minStrength at MODERATE globally.
actions.rationale: The book's expectancy is 0.065R against a 0.05R cost assumption -- roughly 0.015R of genuine edge per trade before any of the above ships. maxTradesPerDay is set to double its default of 5, which scales a barely-positive edge and therefore scales the tax as much as the edge. On minStrength: keep MODERATE. MOMENTUM|MODERATE is 586 closed at +141.84R and PF 1.35 -- more than the entire book's +70.59R -- and seven setups including the profitable TREND_FOLLOW exist only as a MODERATE leg, so a global STRONG gate would not have improved them, it would have deleted them, leaving 51 closed trades in total. STRONG's 0.445R expectancy is real per trade but unreachable at volume.
actions.measurableWhy: Position and trade caps are enforced by the MT5 bridge, entirely outside generateSignal, so the replay's 1411 trades are an uncapped superset of what the live system would take -- it cannot model the caps at all. minStrength is visible to the replay as a strength filter on generateSignal output, but the frequency and sizing half of this action is not.
actions.agreement: risk-and-config raises the maxTradesPerDay-versus-thin-edge point. strength-gate argues explicitly and correctly for holding minStrength at MODERATE, and no analyst proposes reverting it to STRONG. Ranked last because it is a hold-the-line action rather than a source of new R.
actions.risk: Holding frequency and risk low caps the upside if the changes above genuinely work, and lengthens the time needed to accumulate enough live closed trades to verify anything -- which, given a learning file holding 8 win/loss records, is already the binding constraint. Revisit once actions 1-3 have a measured post-change replay behind them.

gate.detail: maxTradesPerDay, riskPercent, maxConcurrentPositions, minStrength is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

blindSpots: No cross-tabulation between dimensions. There is no asset-by-setup, RSI-by-direction, confidence-by-setup or cohort-by-setup breakdown, so overlap between the loss clusters is entirely unmeasured and the R savings from actions 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 are NOT additive. SPX's -85.5R almost certainly contains part of BREAKDOWN's -34.4R and part of the -61.46R below RSI 50. Any arithmetic that sums them overstates the benefit, possibly by a large factor.

Open trades are excluded and close rates vary sharply by bucket: 1411 trades but only 1080 closed; SPX 244 signals to 127 closed (52%), DAILY+H4_AGREE 374 to 214 (57%), conf>=80 360 to 226 (63%), versus H4_ONLY 637 to 589 (92%). If losers close faster than winners -- stops hit before targets -- every low-close-rate bucket is selection-biased toward its losses, which would flatter the case against SPX and against the conflict cohort specifically.

This is one replay over one historical window with no walk-forward, no out-of-sample split and no date-stratified results, so there is no way to separate edge from regime luck. The entire book's profit rides STRONG UPTREND (+158.82R over 667 closed) while every other trend bucket is negative -- the window may simply have been a bull market in BTC and Gold, in which case MOMENTUM's +156.31R is a beta reading rather than an edge, and concentrating the book into it (which actions 1-3 do) increases that exposure rather than reducing it.

Costs are a single flat costAssumptionR of 0.05 with no spread, slippage, swap or per-asset differentiation. SPX, Gold and BTC have materially different real cost structures, and several conclusions turn on margins smaller than plausible cost error -- notably SQUEEZE_BREAKOUT|TRENDING at exactly +0.050 and MODERATE's overall 0.047 expectancy, which is already below the assumed cost.

The replay's trade set is not the set the live system would take. It cannot see confidenceThreshold (so every sub-70-confidence trade among these 1411 is one the live system would never have opened), it cannot see the multi-timeframe agreement in generateSignalMTF, and it cannot see anything the MT5 bridge enforces -- maxConcurrentPositions=3, maxTradesPerDay=10, maxNotionalPct=25, maxLotSize=2. Live results are a capped, filtered subset, and caps bind on exactly the clustered days when the most signals fire, so live sequencing and live R will differ systematically rather than randomly.

Nothing here distinguishes a strategy failure from an execution or instrument-spec failure. SPX at 12.6% win and PF 0.27 on the same logic that yields 33-35% on two other assets is more consistent with a point-value, stop-distance or data defect than with a bad edge, and there is no execution-quality data -- fills, slippage, actual versus intended stop -- to settle it. Only 15 journal entries and 8 live win/loss records exist to check the replay against.

No path or timing data at all: no MAE/MFE, no holding period, no time-of-day or session breakdown, no drawdown sequence, no R-multiple distribution beyond terminal outcomes. So nothing can be said about stop placement, target placement, whether the 31.7% win rate reflects stops that are too tight, or how deep the equity path gets -- which is what 'per unit of risk' would ideally mean and cannot mean here.

The live record and the replay cannot be reconciled. liveState.learning holds 4 setups and 8 win/loss records against the replay's 10 setups and 1411 trades, reports MOMENTUM as net negative where the replay reports it as the only large winner, and contains a setup name (BB_SQUEEZE_WATCH) and an UNATTRIBUTED bucket that appear nowhere in the executed record. Until attribution is consistent there is no way to verify the live system is even running the logic this fact pack replayed -- a precondition for trusting any of the above in production.

No correlation or concurrent-exposure data. BTC, Gold and SPX are scored independently, with nothing on how often positions are open simultaneously or in the same direction, so maxConcurrentPositions=3 could mean three uncorrelated bets or one bet at triple size, and true risk per unit is unknown either way.

The individual trade records were not exploited beyond the aggregates the analysts cite, yet the facts file contains all 1411 of them. Several blind spots above -- close-rate bias, RSI-by-direction, asset-by-setup overlap, R distribution -- are answerable from data already on disk without a new replay. That is the cheapest next measurement and should precede shipping actions 4, 5 and 7.
